text:
Meena: Quick sync — planning the progressive cutover for the EU model switch next week. I want a short, operator-friendly guardrail list + an ops-escrow plan so we can hand control to oncall for immediate rollback. Opinions?
Alex: Agree. Canaries first, then regional ramp. Ops-escrow = temporary feature-flag override held by SREs?
Jordan: Yes — SRE-owned flag with TTL and audit log. Also need automatic rollback triggers so humans don't have to babysit.
Meena: Good. Proposed phases: 1) 1% canary EU only for 2h, 2) 10% for 6h, 3) 50% next day, then full. Canary users are internal + a tiny external cohort.
Luis: Add a safety net: if error_rate > 0.8% OR 99p latency increases by >200ms for 5m, auto-fail to previous model and page oncall.
Rachael: +1. Also require quality checks: sample generation evaluation run (we already have a prompt-suite). If quality regression score drops >3 points abort.
Samir: For ops-escrow I propose RBAC: SRE and EnableOps group can flip the flag. All flips create a support ticket automatically and include `--reason` metadata. TTL default 30m.
Alex: Make TTL configurable per flip. Some emergency rollbacks should allow indefinite but require two approvers (pager + product).
Jordan: Canary routing: use sticky routing per session id so cached KV doesn't skew results. Shadow traffic to previous model for the 10% ramp to compare.
SRE-Bot: deploybot: EU-model-v2 deployed to canary pool at 2024-05-15T09:00Z. Healthcheck started.
Meena: Nice. Who owns the rollout dashboard? Need token-level cost + latency + quality panels visible to oncall and PMs.
Luis: SRE will own infra metrics. Product should own quality panels (we'll surface evals). I'll add a top-line composite signal: "safe_to_ramp" boolean that combines infra + quality thresholds.
Rachael: Define exact thresholds in doc. For quality, use 500 sample prompt-suite and compare BLEU-like / embedding-similarity score. For infra, set error_rate <=0.8% and 99p latency delta <=200ms.
Samir: Rollback play: 1) auto-fail (self-heal), 2) ops flip with TTL, 3) ops flip permanent with two approvers. Document contact list and runbook steps.
Alex: Need a customer opt-out path: some enterprise customers require we exclude their traffic from canaries. Feature flag targeting per-tenant is required.
Meena: Yes — implement tenant opt-out before the 1% canary. Also notify customers in the opt-in bucket 24h before.
Jordan: Also include a graceful degradation policy: if capacity hits 85% GPU util consistently for 5m, start shedding non-critical requests (embeddings batching lower priority).
Luis: Observability: add per-model per-tenant token cost burn rate, and a rolling lookback to detect cost regressions. Alert if cost/token > baseline + 30%.
Rachael: Legal/Compliance: for Private deployments, "ops-escrow" may conflict with customer KMS policies. We'll need an exceptions workflow and explicit customer consent for us to flip flags for private installs.
Meena: Good call. Add an "escrow consent" checkbox in the contract for private customers. For Dedicated/Hosted we can proceed with the default ops-escrow.
Samir: I'll draft the runbook and a short CLI snippet for emergency rollback: `redwood flag set model_switch --value previous --ttl 30m --reason "auto-rollback:latency"`
Alex: Add a dry-run `--notify-only` mode so we can test the orchestration without changing traffic.
Meena: Action items: Samir draft runbook + CLI by EOD tomorrow, Luis add composite signal + dashboard by Tue, Rachael write threshold doc + legal check, Alex coordinate tenant opt-out gating. I'll collate and share final cutover checklist.
Jordan: Suggest a Friday morning small-window for final cutover rehearsal with SRE and CS oncall.
Rachael: I'll schedule rehearsals and prepare the customer comms template.
Meena: Thanks everyone. If no objections, I'll move this into the rollout playbook and create the canary flag with required RBAC. :thumbsup:
Alex: :thumbsup:
SRE-Bot: note: runbook created at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-model-cutover (draft)
